claim: Frame semantics (words evoke frames with named roles; subframes and inheritance change what attaches where) is the founding theory and is operationalised in FrameNet.
agent_test: Compare a frame-listing S1 (roles written out, blanks flagged) vs plain restatement at equal tokens on underspecified tasks.

claim: Supervised frame-semantic role labelling plateaued around 75-77 F1 (argument ID, gold frames) and degrades sharply out of domain; predicted frames cost about 22 F1 versus gold.
agent_test: Not directly testable; use as a ceiling when judging LLM role-filling.

claim: Frame identification is largely solved: few-shot LLMs reach 90.5-94.3 F1 with 50-150 shots; an 8B model fine-tuned reaches 91.7-91.9 accuracy vs supervised best 92.5-92.6.
agent_test: Frame naming alone is not the bottleneck for our agent; spend tokens on role filling.

claim: Role filling is the hard part for LLMs: few-shot argument F1 is 47-59 (FN1.7, 4o-mini to 4o, Devasier) and 67-77 with gold frames (Garat), versus 0.755-0.81 for supervised; fine-tuned LLMs reach 0.785-0.794. The 0.755 vs 0.771 prior-best difference is a table difference (Table 4 fine-tuning vs Table 3 ICL) in the only arXiv version, not a version change.
agent_test: At equal tokens, check whether a model-written role list has missing roles versus a gold list on 30 tasks.

claim: Giving the model frame and role definitions matters enormously in zero-shot: Killing-frame full parse 0.0 F1 without frame info vs 34-48 with it; role F1 for 4o-mini 3.9 vs 39.3.
agent_test: Ablate role definitions in the S1 prompt; measure error on role-omission tasks. Caveat: one paper (Garat et al.), 100 examples.

claim: In-context shots help roles a lot (+30 to +41 F1 on Killing) but frame ID little (+1.4 to +8.7).
agent_test: Few-shot exemplars of filled frames in S1 may beat more definitions; test at matched tokens.

claim: Rare or optional roles are missed: Killing frame Victim 73-83, Killer 48-71, Cause 44-68, Means and Instrument 0-50; unseen frame elements cost -27.0 F1 vs -7.7 for unseen frames.
agent_test: Empty-role hunt should explicitly enumerate peripheral roles (means, instrument, time, place); test recall of planted missing roles.

claim: Output format matters: XML tags 0.342 vs JSON listing only existing roles 0.471 (4o-mini), listing all possible roles 0.440.
agent_test: Compare role-slot formats (JSON-exist vs all-slots) in the frame template.

claim: Frame knowledge is shared and brittle out of domain: Llama YAGS zero-shot 65.4, Artifacts 25.6; GPT-4o YAGS role F1 0.387 vs SEMAFOR 0.570; 296 of 320 shared errors are the same wrong frame.
agent_test: Test the scaffold on tasks outside typical domains; expect frame templates to underperform there.

claim: Prompt granularity effects are small and model-dependent: names only 59.9 zero-shot but 79.1 few-shot; LU definitions help; LLM-written definitions (75.0-80.0) are about as good as gold (78.4-79.3).
agent_test: Let the agent write its own frame definition rather than retrieving FrameNet text; compare.

claim: Injecting FrameNet knowledge by fine-tuning raises event-level inference: CONFER few-shot 0.39 to 0.75 for adapted Llama-3.1-8B; roles-only F1 0.14 to 0.60. Same group wrote both papers.
agent_test: Training-based, not a scaffold; note only as upper bound.

claim: FrameNet annotations in prompts help commonsense multiple choice modestly (GPT-4o-mini SWAG 75.2 to 79.5-80.3) but a WordNet variant does as well (80.3), so the gain is not frame-specific.
agent_test: No plain role-list control exists in the literature (gap 4 open). Run frame-labelled roles vs generic bullet slots vs nothing at equal tokens.

claim: LLM-assisted frame annotation saves little time (14.96 vs 12.97 min per sentence) and machine core-role coverage is poor (34.2% vs 95.8% human; hybrid 90.7%).
agent_test: Do not trust the model's own role enumeration without a check pass; test with a verifier step.

claim: Wording and frame effects on human reasoning are fragile: Steen et al. (N=253-1026) found no metaphor effect; Thibodeau and Boroditsky pooled N=876 w=.14; Loftus-Palmer verb effect not found overall (N=1204), only a moderated one.
agent_test: Test sensitivity of agent answers to paraphrased task framings.

claim: Classic equivalent-framing effects (Asian disease) replicate in Many Labs 1 at about 53-67% of original size, but may shrink when numeric quantifiers are read in context.
agent_test: Snippet-level only; verify before use.

claim: LLMs show framing effects and debiasing helps: DeFrame cuts BBQ framing disparity 92% on 8 models (3B-14B); CogBias framing accuracy 35.6% to 41.4%; risk shifts up to +1.84 in championship framings. But in FRAGILE (7-8B open models, flip rate 28.6% average) text-level value-anchor prompts failed to suppress flips and sometimes raised them; only a hidden-state method cut them (Llama value-tinted 39.9% to 11.9%). A neutral re-framing step on frontier models is untested.
agent_test: Ask the same task under gain and loss frames; measure answer flips; test a neutral re-framing step at equal tokens.

claim: Underspecified inputs: asking recovers much of the lost performance (Ambig-SWE up to 74% gain, 80% of Full recovered by Sonnet 3.5/Haiku 3.5, 89% by Sonnet 4; UA-Multi 69.4 vs Full 70.8 and UA-Single 61.2 with Sonnet 4.5). Unprompted detection is weak (Ambig-SWE accuracy 0.48-0.74 neutral prompt; false positive rate up to 0.95) and a separate gate agent beats an inline reminder by 8.2 points at about 1.5-1.7x cost per task. Tool agents invent missing arguments (56% of problematic real queries miss key information).
agent_test: Test a separate missing-role gate then ask-or-assume step on underspecified tasks; compare against a generic 'what is missing' gate at equal tokens; track false positives and cost (about $3.50 vs $2.03 per task in UA).

claim: A fixed slot checklist that picks which missing item to ask about raises coverage of hidden requirements well above free-form prompting: ReqElicitGym (101 scenarios, GPT-5.1) IRE 0.13 plain, 0.52 best prompt baseline, 0.41 with the ontology alone, 0.69 full OntoAgent.
agent_test: Compare a task-specific slot list with a generic 'what is missing' prompt on coverage of hidden requirements at equal tokens.

claim: Forcing all FrameNet core and non-core elements into a requirements prompt makes outputs longer and more stable (R01 44 vs 5-7 requirements; R02 26 vs 10-13) with small Llama 3.2 models, but accuracy was not measured.
agent_test: Do not count this as accuracy evidence; add a correctness rating if reused.

claim: Without being told, agents rarely ask and tend to invent a missing tool argument; an ask-when-needed prompt raises asking-correctly rates (gpt-4o 0.52 to 0.90; o3-mini 0.00 to 0.78) but final-answer gains are smaller (gpt-4o 0.34 to 0.36).
agent_test: After the missing-role flag, require either an ask or an explicitly labelled assumption; measure final-answer accuracy, not only asking rate.

claim: Humans silently complete unstated roles from background frames or scripts and later cannot separate inferred from stated content (Bower, Black and Turner 1979, second-hand; Fillmore birthday-party example via Petruck 1996). No numbers obtained.
agent_test: Require the agent to tag each filled role as stated or inferred.

claim: No study of 2026 frontier models reports per-role F1 for peripheral roles, no plain role-list control against FrameNet prompts exists, and no direct test of a frame-then-find-blanks scaffold on general reasoning exists.
agent_test: Own pilot: frame-labelled roles vs generic slots vs plain restatement at equal tokens on underspecified and multi-constraint tasks.
